A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same African NLP survey. Their main text, Figures 1-7, Tables 1-4, and Appendices A-E are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative analyses of 734 manually annotated papers and a 50-paper evaluation of automatic filtering in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 reports original quantitative analyses of 884 manually annotated papers and a 100-paper evaluation of automatic filtering in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o screening component changes from general AI classification to an explicit NLP-relevance decision rule covering speech, multimodal language tasks, and related applications (Appendix B, Listing 1). The overall retrieval, screening, and manual-coding pipeline remains.

E1.justification: Reported coverage increases slightly from 2,271 to 2,275 African languages and dialects (Section 4.2). The filtering evaluation also changes its target from general AI relevance to NLP relevance. The survey retains its broad African NLP domain.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing methods against a proposed model or screening system. Added models in the resource catalogs are surveyed resources, not experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Language search terms expand from 53 NLLB-200 languages to 2,290 ISO-coded Glottolog languages, and searched venues add FAccT and RANLP. The analyzed corpus changes from 734 to 884 papers. Appendix B also increases the balanced filtering audit from 25 to 50 papers per category.

E4.justification: Appendix B revises the screening error analysis for the new NLP-relevance criterion. The larger manual audit reports one false negative, replacing the earlier AI-filter audit whose errors included computer-vision papers. No ablation or prompt-sensitivity experiment is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report descriptive counts, percentages, and filtering accuracy without repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates. The increased audit sample size changes the evaluation design, not uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Numerous corpus findings change: the publication peak moves from 2023 to 2024, the leading country pair changes from Mozambique/Nigeria to Mozambique/Uganda, and dataset-creation papers increase from 350 to 401. Appendix B reports 92% versus 99% filtering accuracy under different criteria and samples, not a controlled performance gain. Tables 3-4 add resource entries.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, or proofs. Added descriptions of techniques such as meta-learning remain conceptual literature summaries.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory goals, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a comprehensive overview, an accessible research resource, and identification of open issues. Updating the corpus size does not redefine the central claims about progress and uneven coverage.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning missing language metadata, testing only one filtering prompt, and the absence of systematic social and ethical assessment. It also explains the inclusion of African-accented European languages. The principal interpretations and future directions remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future dataset release; v3 states that both data and code are public and supplies repository access information. v3 also documents the expanded filtering prompt and the ISO 639-3 restriction on Glottolog search languages, substantially improving reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Ghanaian surveys and explicit comparisons with tool-focused, bootstrapping, and translation-bias surveys. Appendix D adds a meta-learning synthesis, and the resource catalogs gain references. These extend the literature discussion while retaining the continental landscape positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and terminology corrections, expands related-survey explanations, and organizes limitations into labeled paragraphs. The section sequence and most of the narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redesigned as a full-width horizontal flowchart. Other plots receive revised axes and category labels, Listing 1 expands to full width, and resource tables gain rows. The overall two-column design and figure/table inventory remain.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the survey's collection procedure and reproducibility: replacing the 53-language query list with 2,290 Glottolog languages addresses restrictive retrieval, while explicit NLP screening and reported public code/data access make the evidence easier to assess. Expanded limitations improve qualification of the findings. Bookkeeping remains imperfect: Table 2 reports 27,617 retrieved papers whereas Section 3 and Figure 2 report 27,593. This localized inconsistency does not outweigh the methodological and transparency gains.
